simple.meaning: דָּלַג (dâlag) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to spring.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 5 times in 2 Samuel, Psalms, Song of Solomon, Isaiah, Zephaniah, beginning at 2 Samuel 22:30. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דָּלַג (H1801) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: דָּלַג (dâlag) / H1801 is traced through 2 Samuel 22:30, Psalms 18:30, Song of Songs 2:8, Isaiah 35:6 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H1801. dalag [ דָּלַג ] verb leap ( Late Hebrew spring over, skip (a verse), omit) — Qal Participle דּוֺלֵג Zeph 1:9 leap , with article one leaping עלהַֿמִּפְתָּן ; ᵐ5 1Sam 5:5 ὑπερβαίνοντες ὑπερβαίνουσιν = יִדְלֹ֑גוּ דָּלֹג compare Dr. Pi`el Imperfect יְדַלֵּג Isa 35:6 ; אֲדַלֶּגֿ Psa 18:30 = 2Sam 22:30 ; Participle מְדַלֵּג Song 2:8 ; — leap, leap over with accusative שׁוּר Psa 18:30 = 2Sam 22:30 ; absolute leap as the stag , ׳יְד מִּסֵּחַ כָּאַיָּל Isa 35:6 ; followed by על of locality Song 2:8 (|| מְקַמֵּץ ).

occurrences.englishText: For by you, I run against a troop.
As for God, his way is perfect.
Then the lame man will leap like a deer,
In that day, I will punish all those who leap over the threshold, who fill their master’s house with violence and deceit.
